\section{Preliminaries}
A set $M$ of $m$ chores $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ is allocated to a set $N$ of $n$ agents $1,\ldots,n$.
We will use ``item'' and ``chore'' interchangeably in this paper to refer to an element in $M$.
Each agent $i$'s cost function $c_i:2^M\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$ is additive:
$$c_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S}c_i(\{g\}).$$

EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.reason: This is the source EFX predicate applied to the instance's additive cost function. The exact empty-bundle alternative and one-item-removal inequality are independently exposed by EFXForChores.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.reason: The paper's allocation convention allocates the chore set among agents. This predicate specializes the separately reviewed complete-allocation condition to the instance's declared chore set; it adds no source-side feasibility condition.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.reason: This specializes the source Pareto-optimality definition to all chores and the instance's additive cost. It is exactly the source notion, with feasibility supplied by the allocation convention.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.AdditiveChoreInst.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.Allocation.reason: The source writes an allocation as a tuple of one bundle for each agent. The Lean definition is that agent-indexed tuple; complete allocation is reviewed separately.

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsCanonicalSmallC.label: IsCanonicalSmallChoreAllocation
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsCanonicalSmallC.reason: The definition requires a complete allocation, exact quotas, and exactly min(quota, own-small-count) own-small chores for every agent, matching the source canonical-allocation definition.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsCanonicalSmallC.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsLargeChore.reason: The source says a chore is large for an agent exactly when its cost is r. The Lean predicate is that equality.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsLargeChore.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsOneOrRChoreCost.label: IsOneOrRChoreCost
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsOneOrRChoreCost.reason: The source's normalized bi-valued model says every individual chore cost is either 1 or r. The Lean predicate is exactly that pointwise disjunction.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsOneOrRChoreCost.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallChore.reason: The source says a chore is small for an agent exactly when its cost is 1. The Lean predicate is that equality.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallChore.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallForAtLeast.reason: The source defines M34 as chores whose small-agent set has cardinality at least three. The Lean predicate is exactly that cardinality condition.

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallForAtMostO.label: IsSmallForAtMostOne
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallForAtMostO.reason: For an M01 chore, the source defines the small-agent set to have cardinality at most one. The Lean predicate states that same finite-cardinality condition.

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSmallForExactly.reason: The source defines M2 as chores whose small-agent set has cardinality exactly two. The Lean predicate is that exact cardinality condition.

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSuperCanonicalS.label: IsSuperCanonicalSmallChoreAllocation
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSuperCanonicalS.reason: The library definition combines canonicality with the source short-agent versus long-agent cost gap. The paper interface supplies the source's cardinality-based short and long sets.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsSuperCanonicalS.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.IsTriValuedChoreC.reason: The source defines tri-valued costs by three nonnegative constants with every pointwise item cost in their set. The Lean predicate is that exact condition.

EconCSLib.FairDivision.ParetoDominatesFo.reason: The displayed Pareto-dominance definition says that an improvement weakly decreases every agent's cost and strictly decreases one cost. The Lean declaration is exactly that two-part condition for an improvement and a current allocation.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.ParetoDominatesFo.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.ParetoOptimalForC.reason: The source forbids an allocation that weakly decreases every agent's cost and strictly decreases one. The Lean definition states that condition over the complete-allocation convention.
EconCSLib.FairDivision.ParetoOptimalForC.validator: Codex HT26 raw source-to-library semantic reviewer

EconCSLib.FairDivision.additiveChoreCost.reason: The Lean definition sums the source's singleton costs over the finite bundle, exactly as the displayed additive-cost equation.
